# Appendix {.unnumbered}

This appendix gathers the material behind the chapters: the data files and where they came from, the scripts that draw each figure, how the AI models in Chapter 2 were asked, credits for the photographs and documents, sources for further reading, and the software used.

```{r}
#| label: setupappendix
#| code-summary: "Show the setup code"

## formatted tables
library(gt)
```

## Data files

Every data figure in this document is drawn from a file in the project's `data/` folder. The table lists each file, the chapters that use it, what it holds and where it came from.

```{r}
#| label: datafiles
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

## the list of data files, with their sources
datafiles <- read.csv("data/appendix_data_files.csv")
## add the size of each file, in kilobytes
datafiles$kb <- round(file.size(file.path("data", datafiles$file)) / 1024)
## show it
gt(datafiles[, c("file", "chapter", "holds", "source", "kb")]) |>
  cols_label(file = "File", chapter = "Chapter", holds = "What it holds",
             source = "Source", kb = "Size (KB)") |>
  tab_source_note(source_note = "Files are in the data/ folder of the project.")
```

Two other sources are read directly by the scripts rather than stored in `data/`. The climate of the 24 cities in Chapter 2 comes from WorldClim version 2.1, at 2.5 arc-minute resolution. The biome boundaries in Chapter 7 come from the `whittakerr` package, and the soil texture classes from the USDA class outlines distributed with the `ggtern` package.

## Figure scripts

Each figure is drawn by a script in the project's `R/` folder. The chapters run the script when the document is built, so every figure is redrawn from its data each time.

```{r}
#| label: scripts
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

## the scripts, what they make, and what they need
scripts <- read.csv("data/appendix_figure_scripts.csv")
## show it, grouped by chapter
gt(scripts, groupname_col = "chapter") |>
  cols_label(script = "Script", makes = "What it draws", uses = "What it uses") |>
  tab_source_note(source_note = "Scripts are in the R/ folder of the project.")
```

One script, `ch02_llm_elicit.R`, doesn't draw a figure. It asks the AI models their questions and saves the answers. It was run once, and its results are kept in `llm_comfort_thresholds_24cities.csv`, so the document can be rebuilt without asking the models again.

## Asking the machines

Chapter 2 used three AI models as instruments for eliciting tacit temperature scales. The models were Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Anthropic), GPT-5 mini (OpenAI) and Gemini 3.8 Flash (Google), called from R through the `ellmer` package on 3 November 2026. Each model was asked the same question three times for each of 24 cities, giving 216 sets of answers. The answers came back as four numbers in a fixed structure, one for each word.

The question, exactly as sent, with the city and country filled in, was:

```text
Think about ordinary people who have lived in <city>, <country> for many years.
In everyday conversation, at what outdoor air temperatures (daytime, in degrees
Fahrenheit) do they start to describe the weather as 'cold', 'chilly', 'warm'
and 'hot'? Give typical local thresholds, as whole numbers, for their own sense
of the words -- not a universal standard.
```

The models are treated as a way to reach what is written about how people talk, not as an authority on it. Their answers agreed with one another closely, which says they share a source more than it proves the source is right. A check against how real residents use the words would be the natural next step.

## Photographs, documents and the cover

The photograph of Hōkūleʻa arriving in Palau (Chapter 9) is mine, taken in April 2007, as is the printed schedule of events shown beside it. The optical-mark-reader request form in Chapter 6 is from my own files, from my years teaching introductory biology at the University of Hawaiʻi; the contact details on it are covered. The cover image was generated with an AI image tool.

## Software

The figures were drawn in R. The table lists the packages the scripts load, found by reading the scripts themselves, with the version used for this build.

```{r}
#| label: software
#| code-summary: "Show the code"

## read every figure script and find the packages it uses
code <- unlist(lapply(list.files("R", pattern = "\\.R$", full.names = TRUE), readLines, warn = FALSE))
found <- c(regmatches(code, gregexpr("(?<=library\\()[A-Za-z0-9.]+", code, perl = TRUE)),
           regmatches(code, gregexpr("[A-Za-z0-9.]+(?=::)", code, perl = TRUE)),
           regmatches(code, gregexpr("(?<=package = ')[A-Za-z0-9.]+", code, perl = TRUE)))
pkgs <- sort(setdiff(unique(unlist(found)), c("base", "stats", "utils", "grDevices", "graphics", "tools")))
## their versions, with R itself at the top
software <- data.frame(package = c("R", pkgs),
                       version = c(paste(R.version$major, R.version$minor, sep = "."),
                                   vapply(pkgs, function(p) as.character(packageVersion(p)), character(1))))
## show it
gt(software) |> cols_label(package = "Package", version = "Version")
```
